title: New Work Order shows the No Charge checkbox at the bottom with its tooltip
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, not flagged, with one asset, asset 1.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Work Order.
  2. Pick customer A.
  3. Hover over the info icon next to "No Charge".
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Work Order window opens.

Step 2:

  • At the bottom of the window, below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and a divider, an unticked "No Charge" checkbox shows with an info icon.

Step 3:

  • The tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category."

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11759 (Story 2, An internal or no-charge work order from creation to Close)

  • S2-R2: “In the New Work Order dialog (New Work Order only; Edit Work Order, which shares the dialog, is unchanged), picking a customer without the flag shows, at the bottom of the dialog below the "Asset Here?" checkbox and separated from it by a divider, an unticked checkbox "No Charge" with an info icon whose tooltip reads "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." Ticking it reveals the required select "Category" listing the active No Charge categories, empty by default; Save is refused with the field message "Pick a category" until one is picked. When the category requires the original work order, the select "Original work order" appears under it (the customer's invoiced and closed work orders at the locations the user has access to, those on the same asset first, each as number, date and first line, and "Not in ShopView" under Other), optional here, with the helper "Which earlier work order this job comes from, or Not in ShopView, and the line on it. The line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers. Optional here, required at Close."; once a work order is picked, the optional select "Original line" lists its lines (number, title, technician). The checkbox is hidden when the selected customer is an internal customer and for users without 'See Financial Data'. Ticked, the work order is created No Charge with that category. It works whether or not any customer is flagged. As soon as a work order or a line is picked, the line "Original technician: [names]" (or "Original technician: none") shows under the selects, so a wrong attribution is seen and corrected by picking the line before anything is saved.”
  • User Feedback Summary: “No Charge info icon (New Work Order) | "Warranty, goodwill or comeback work. Closes without an invoice; parts cost posts to the expense account of the category." | Tooltip on the info icon”
  • Feature Overview: “No Charge is a mark with a category. A whole work order on a regular customer can be No Charge (the checkbox at creation, Convert to No Charge later, Convert to Billable back), and so can a single line of a billable work order (Mark as No Charge in the line's three-dots menu, or the No Charge checkbox in Edit Line and New Line; Story 12). Both carry one No Charge category from the shop's list (Warranty, Goodwill, Comeback to start, plus the shop's own) and, on categories that require it, the original work order the job comes from and, optionally, the original line on it, which sets the original technician. Categories are shop-managed: Administration > Service > Internal Work Orders holds two lists, Internal categories and No Charge categories; a category has a name, a QuickBooks expense account per connected location and, on No Charge, the flag Requires the original work order (on for Warranty and Comeback). Categories are archived, never deleted, so old work orders and reports keep theirs. The same accounts show on Settings > Integrations > QuickBooks > ShopView Accounts as one row per category; editing either place writes the same mapping. Nothing is created in QuickBooks.”
